cells.tense: The ruling has come down, and the pen rests in the hand now.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Set down the one arrangement between you and someone else that has finished serving its purpose — honoured past its time, still coasting. Keep what still holds. Nothing needs saying about the reason.
cells.core:
You can carry a feeling the whole way through and still make the fair call at the end of it. Not one person's hurt gets extra weight for being loud, and not yours either. The ruling waits for the feeling to finish, which is exactly what makes it hold.

On undecided ground there is one old agreement to put down — something between people that made sense once and has been coasting since. Letting it go costs the ease of something you've honoured past its time. The people inside it already know it's finished; setting it down says the same thing back to them, without a single word about why. What stays in your hands is the part still worth keeping.
cells.sheetLine: You feel all of it and still call it fair.
cells.verb: feeling what is fair between people and calling it
cells.place: the open, uncommitted ground before anything has been chosen

cells.tense: A verdict is being drafted for a day that hasn't shown up yet.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: When something between you and another person comes in hot, hold it a full day before weighing it. Carry it as weight, not as a case to close, and rule on nothing until the day is out.
cells.core:
Rulings are landing before the feelings they are about have finished moving. Somebody is still raw, and the question of how much room that gets has already been answered. On ground where nothing has been chosen, this shows up as bracing: each open possibility weighed and sentenced in advance, and it lands on the people near you like a court they wandered into.

Strength that holds does not need the answer early. Take the thing that reaches you and carry it for a day with no wall decided for it yet — weight in the hands, nothing built. Carrying it settles nothing, and that is the whole point. Tomorrow the same call is still yours, and whoever it concerns has room to take it in.

cells.tense: The door had already shut, and the standing there continued anyway.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Put an unfair situation onto paper in the order it unfolded — no feeling words on the page. Read it back once and set it aside.
cells.core:
Something between people has gone crooked and nobody is weighing it — not you, not the other party. It just sits there leaning, and the people near it can feel the tilt. The call belongs to you, and the version of you that makes calls like this is still parked at a door that closed, holding the handle.

Nerve won't fetch it back. Method doesn't ask for nerve. Put the unfair thing on paper in the order it happened, no feeling words anywhere, and read it back to yourself once. You're not settling anything — just putting down what occurred. Half the call is already sitting there in your handwriting, and the page doesn't need you anywhere but here.

cells.tense: The pen is down on the table, in a room that is being written anyway.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: At the next disagreement near you, hear the whole of it as a student — all the way through, before stepping in to even anything.
cells.core:
Things stay level among the people near you because you keep them level — a word dropped in, a weight shifted. Ask you, and you happened to be standing close. That keeping is real and it has a keeper, and those being kept level have known the truth of it for a long while.

Go back to the plain form of it: the student. At the next disagreement you're near, take it in all the way to the end as someone learning what it is, before you reach for the smoothing. You'll catch the part you usually walk straight past, and the evening-out you do gets seen from inside, by the one doing it. The situation stays exactly as it is. The one holding it level stops being a stranger to the work.
